name: Forecast liquidity for each client portfolio
summary: Every week the total portfolio team rolls forward a cash and liquidity forecast for each of the five client portfolios and the pools: client contributions and withdrawals, capital calls and distributions on private commitments, margin and currency hedge settlements, hedge fund dealing and fees, against the stock of liquid assets. Risk then tests whether liquid assets cover stressed outflows with a liquidity coverage ratio, and the portfolio manager decides whether any client risks becoming a forced seller. The work is spreadsheet-heavy and depends on inputs from cash operations, private markets operations and clients; uncertain general partner call timing and late warnings of large client payments are the main sources of forecast error.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about 240 staff that invests about $79 billion for a few public pension plans and an insurance board through pooled funds and segregated accounts, on a cost recovery basis.
baseline.notes: Five client portfolios and four pools in 2021, with most private assets in segregated client accounts, so calls are forecast by client account. Leverage was first applied in 2022, adding margin and financing needs. Daily cash funding and margin calls are separate processes.

unit_of_work: one weekly liquidity forecast across all portfolios
trigger: The weekly cycle starts on Monday once the prior week's cash and positions are reconciled and the cash, capital call, distribution, client flow and hedge fund teams have updated their forecasts.
end_state: The liquidity report is published, any low-coverage actions are sent to rebalancing and overlays, month-end figures go to reporting, and the model version is archived.

volume.seasonality: Even through the year; extra runs and closer monitoring in market stress such as March 2020 and 2022.

evidence.note: Weekly cadence from the organisation file; the insurance client's policy requires at least monthly monitoring.

steps.name: Pull opening cash, positions and last week's flows
steps.description: On Monday morning a total portfolio analyst pulls reconciled cash and positions for each client portfolio and pool from the book of record, custodian and unitholder register, and the actual flows of the past week: client contributions and withdrawals, capital calls, distributions, margin, settlements and fees.

error.defect_description: A late-booked flow or unreconciled cash break is carried into the opening position.

evidence.note: Weekly cash reviews built from bank and ledger data are common practice; weekly cadence at this firm is from the organisation file. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Compare last week's forecast with actual flows
steps.description: The analyst compares last week's forecast with what actually happened by flow type and client, explains the main differences (a call arriving early, a client changing a withdrawal date, a margin spike) and adjusts the assumptions behind the next forecast.

error.defect_description: A variance is explained wrongly and the assumption is not corrected.

evidence.note: Forecast review against actuals with manual adjustments is described; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Get the cash team's short-term projection
steps.description: The cash and collateral analyst exports the daily cash projection for the next two to four weeks by account: trade settlements, unit transactions, scheduled wires, manager fees and foreign exchange settlements, and sends it to the analyst.

error.defect_description: A large scheduled payment is left out of the export.

evidence.note: Hand-off follows the organisation file's daily cash process; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Update expected client contributions and withdrawals
steps.description: The analyst updates each client's expected contributions and withdrawals (pension payroll funding, benefit payments, insurance fund set-asides) from the client cash instruction log and the clients' own forecasts, and marks large or uncertain amounts.

error.defect_description: A client flow is entered in the wrong week or portfolio.

next.condition: large or uncertain flows to confirm

evidence.note: Client fund outflows are one of the outflows in the model manager's liquidity coverage ratio; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Confirm large client flows with relationship managers
steps.description: For large or uncertain flows, the analyst asks the client relationship manager, who checks with the client's finance staff whether the amount and date still hold. Clients do not always warn early about large payments.

evidence.note: Author estimate; the organisation file notes the forecast depends on clients warning early.

steps.name: Get capital call notices and general partner guidance
steps.description: A private markets operations analyst sends the list of capital call and distribution notices received but not yet paid, with due dates usually about ten business days out, and any guidance general partners have given about upcoming calls or exits.

error.defect_description: A notice received by email is not yet in the system.

evidence.note: Hand-off follows the organisation file's capital call process; notice period as in the capital call workflow. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Update capital call and distribution projections
steps.description: The analyst updates expected calls and distributions on each fund's unfunded commitment by client account: known notices for the next two weeks, then model-based estimates by month for a year. Call timing is uncertain, so the projection is often revised.

error.defect_description: Call timing or size is wrong, so actual calls differ from the forecast.

evidence.note: Model-based call and distribution projections are standard; executives call capital calls largely unpredictable. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Project margin, collateral and currency hedge settlements
steps.description: The cash and collateral analyst estimates variation margin on futures, settlements of maturing currency forwards at their roll dates and collateral on swaps, including what a sharp fall in the Canadian dollar or in equities would demand in cash.

error.defect_description: A forward roll or a large futures position is left out.

evidence.note: Futures are margined in cash daily, currency forwards all mature within a year, and variation margin on uncleared trades is called daily; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Add hedge fund dealing, pool flows and fees
steps.description: The analyst adds expected hedge fund redemption proceeds and holdbacks, subscriptions with notice deadlines, planned pool rebalancing flows and quarterly manager fee payments.

error.defect_description: A redemption holdback is treated as cash on the dealing date.

evidence.note: Flows follow the organisation file's process map; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Build the base-case forecast
steps.description: The analyst rolls forward sources and uses for each client portfolio and pool, by week for 13 weeks and by month for a year, against the stock of liquid assets (cash, treasury bills, government bonds and repo capacity), in the forecast workbook.

error.defect_description: A formula or mapping error double counts a flow or assigns it to the wrong client.

evidence.note: Spreadsheet-based forecasts are common; the model manager aims to balance enough liquidity against idle capital. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Run stressed outflows and the liquidity coverage ratio
steps.description: A senior risk manager runs the stressed case: high-quality liquid assets compared with net outflows from client withdrawals, rebalancing needs, capital calls and currency hedge settlements under past stresses and a one-in-20-year event, for each client portfolio and pool.

error.defect_description: A stress assumption is applied to the wrong client.

control.basis: The model manager liquidity risk framework: liquidity coverage ratio under past stresses and a one-in-20-year event

evidence.note: The ratio's definition, outflow types and stress horizons are stated in the 2021 and 2022 annual reports; weekly running is an author estimate.

steps.name: Portfolio manager reviews the forecast
steps.description: A total portfolio manager reviews each client's base case and coverage, looks for weeks where outflows bunch, and decides whether any client is at risk of becoming a forced seller and needs action, or whether the numbers need correcting first.

evidence.note: Avoiding forced selling is the model manager's stated aim; observed practice keeps liquid assets for potential cash demands. Shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Agree actions for low coverage
steps.description: The head of total portfolio management agrees what to do: raise cash in fixed income or money markets, slow rebalancing, reduce overlay or hedge exposure, use repo, or ask the relationship manager to warn the client.

control.basis: Liquidity escalation thresholds in the liquidity risk framework

evidence.note: The model manager used alternative sources of liquidity in 2022; plans keep contingency liquidity for severe events. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Write commentary and publish the liquidity report
steps.description: The analyst writes a one-page summary per client and pool (large upcoming flows, coverage, actions) and publishes the report to the CIO, total portfolio team, cash team, risk and client relationship managers, saving it for the monthly risk report.

error.defect_description: Commentary does not match the final numbers.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Discuss at the weekly total portfolio meeting
steps.description: The portfolio manager takes the team through liquidity alongside rebalancing and overlays, agrees which clients' flows can be used to rebalance and which overlay or hedge changes are needed.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Send action requests to rebalancing and overlays
steps.description: The portfolio manager sends requests to the rebalancing and overlay work: use a client inflow to rebalance, raise cash ahead of a large withdrawal, or cut a hedge or futures exposure to free margin.

evidence.note: Overlays and fund flows are used to rebalance without selling physical assets; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Provide month-end coverage for risk and client reports
steps.description: In the week after month end the risk manager sends each client's coverage figures and commentary to the monthly risk report and client reporting, as clients' policies require liquidity coverage to be monitored at least monthly.

control.basis: Client statement of investment policies (The insurance client): liquidity coverage monitored at least monthly

evidence.note: Monthly monitoring requirement is stated; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Save the model version and log assumption changes
steps.description: The analyst saves the dated version of the forecast workbook in the controlled folder and records changes to assumptions or formulas in the change log reviewed under the firm's spreadsheet controls.

control.basis: End-user computing controls over key spreadsheets in the SOC 1 control environment

evidence.note: The model manager obtained a SOC 1 report on its controls in 2021; times are author estimates.

exceptions.name: Large client flow to confirm
exceptions.description: A large or uncertain contribution or withdrawal is checked with the client through the relationship manager, which can take a day or two.

exceptions.name: Coverage below warning level
exceptions.description: A client's stressed coverage falls below the warning level, usually from bunched capital calls, a large withdrawal or margin in volatile markets, and the head of total portfolio management agrees actions.

exceptions.name: Forecast errors corrected
exceptions.description: The portfolio manager finds a mapping or formula error and sends the forecast back.

exceptions.name: Liquidity-driven rebalancing or overlay change
exceptions.description: The forecast leads to a request to use flows for rebalancing or to reduce overlay or hedge exposure.

exceptions.name: Market stress
exceptions.description: In stress such as March 2020, margin and hedge settlements jump, funding markets tighten and the forecast is rerun more often than weekly.

pain_points.description: General partners' call timing is uncertain and notices arrive with about ten business days' warning, so the call projection is revised every week.

evidence.note: Executives describe projecting capital calls as largely unpredictable.

pain_points.description: Clients do not always warn early about large payments, so large flows have to be chased through relationship managers.

evidence.note: Author judgement; noted in the organisation file's process description.

pain_points.description: The forecast is assembled in spreadsheets from several teams' exports, which invites mapping and formula errors and makes the run slow.

evidence.note: Practitioners describe manual Excel forecasting with many adjustments.

pain_points.description: Derivative margin and hedge settlements can demand large amounts of cash within a day or two in stress, when funding markets are also strained.

evidence.note: Large liquidity demands in March 2020; margin due within one or two days; regulators ask for margin call stress tests.

assumptions: Unit of work is the weekly forecast across all portfolios, as in the organisation file; daily cash funding and daily margin calls are separate processes that feed this one.
private_markets_ops_analyst and client_relationship_manager are organisation file roles not listed on this process_map entry; they supply inputs.
The model manager describes its liquidity coverage ratio but not its warning thresholds or how often it is run; a weekly run alongside the forecast is assumed.
Shares of weeks with escalation (12%), corrections (10%) and follow-up requests (25%) and all times are author estimates.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's ranges.

sources.title: The model manager Gains 5.4% in 2020
sources.supports: Managing total portfolio liquidity to avoid being a forced seller; clients had sufficient liquidity in 2020; leverage not yet used but under discussion with clients and the board; board met more often by video in spring 2020 to review liquidity and risk; external managers cut from 200 to 124.

sources.title: Insurance fund (The insurance client web page with the statement of investment policies and procedures)
sources.supports: The model manager is sole investment manager; the model manager establishes benchmarks and relative return and risk targets for each strategy; liquidity coverage monitored at least monthly; derivatives may be used to manage allocations including rebalancing; leverage target 10% within 5% to 15%; currency exposure handled under the insurance client or the model manager policies; performance, risk and compliance reviewed at least quarterly; SIPP reviewed every fiscal year.

sources.title: The pension client 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: New strategic asset allocation approved April 2021 and implemented by the model manager over four years, adding portfolio leverage; futures subject to daily cash margining; foreign exchange forwards used for passive and active hedging; currency forwards notional of about $6.5 billion at end 2021, all maturing within one year. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: Alternative Assets and Risk Management: Insights into Practices Observed from FSRA's Review of Six Large Public Sector Pension Plans in Ontario
sources.publisher: Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario
sources.supports: Observed practice: a liquidity management process keeps high-quality liquid assets available for potential cash demands over conservative horizons, allowing for severe events that freeze funding markets; centralised risk control separate from investment teams; plans faced significant liquidity demands in March 2020. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: COVID-19 crisis: Liquidity management at Canada's largest public pension funds (Staff Analytical Note 2021-11, abstract page)
sources.supports: The eight largest Canadian public pension funds faced large demands for liquidity in March 2020, were generally resilient and relied heavily on core funding markets.

sources.title: One in five US pension plans lack adverse scenario liquidity (survey news release)
sources.supports: Survey of 50 senior US pension executives (November 2024): 22% lack liquidity for adverse scenarios, 60% say liquidity could become a problem in extreme cases; projecting capital calls is largely unpredictable.

sources.title: Overestimating Liquidity Needs Can Undercut the Return Potential of US Pension Plans
sources.supports: Liquidity demand from benefits, capital calls (historically 25% to 35% of normal in volatile markets) and rebalancing (3% to 7% of assets a year); supply to demand ratio of 2x to 3x; stress assumes no distributions and a two-year down market.

sources.title: Fundamentals and Best Practices of Cash Forecasting
sources.supports: Practitioners review cash positions weekly, often in Excel dashboards with many manual adjustments; data comes from bank portals, payables and receivables and business units; short-term forecasts are the most accurate.

sources.title: The Evolution of the Yale Model for Institutional Investing
sources.supports: Takahashi-Alexander model projects contributions, distributions and NAV per quarter from rate of contribution, commitment, fund life, bow factor, growth and yield; widely used by limited partners; deterministic, so Monte Carlo is suggested.

sources.title: Guideline: Margin Requirements for Non-Centrally Cleared Derivatives (2020)
sources.publisher: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions
sources.supports: Variation margin called daily with a minimum transfer amount of at most $750,000 and exchanged within two business days; initial margin phased in from September 2021 and September 2022; physically settled FX forwards and swaps excluded from margin requirements but counted toward thresholds.

sources.title: Dutch pension funds can meet margin calls on derivatives, but depend on functioning money markets
sources.supports: Pension funds must post collateral within one or two days of a derivative losing value; they draw on cash, repo and money market funds; stress tests used sharp interest rate and currency shocks.

sources.title: Liquidity Preparedness for Margin and Collateral Calls: Final report
sources.supports: Non-bank participants should include margin and collateral calls in liquidity risk management, stress test them under extreme but plausible conditions, hold sufficient liquid assets and keep collateral processes resilient; cites March 2020 and the September 2022 LDI fund episode.

sources.title: The rule for rebalancing the equity share in the Government Pension Fund Global
sources.supports: Large rebalancing trades are spread over time and use fund inflows to cut transaction costs; band-based triggers.

sources.title: Overlay program with an OCIO (insight article)
sources.supports: Futures overlays keep allocations on target without selling physical assets, useful with illiquid assets; swaps for precise hedges; collateral pools back overlay exposure.

sources.title: Asset Manager's Guide to SOC 1 (June 2017)
sources.supports: Baseline control objective: trades properly authorised, settled and recorded in line with portfolio guidelines and account restrictions; block orders allocated by approved methods. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.
